weather.json.description: Open-Meteo ECMWF IFS daily precipitation_sum (425 days: 365 warm-up + 60 eval) plus 60 Single-Runs forecast inputs.

sources.availableAt: closeTime (candle period end); a candle is immutable once finalized. Exact publication lag is not recorded and is immaterial: strategies use candles with closeTime strictly before cutoff.
sources.note: YES means close > open compared exactly (decimal strings), per spec. NEARUSDT is a Tether-stablecoin pair, not fiat USD.

sources.availableAt: fetched 2026-11-05 (post-evaluation). Resolution truth = pinned model/grid + captured response, not a station observation.
sources.note: Outcome YES means daily precipitation_sum >= 1.0 mm over the Asia/Jakarta (WIB) day. IFS 9 km analysis is gridded model output, not an official station reading.

Reanalysis for a past day can be revised after the fact. The value fetched today for a past date is not proven to equal the value available at the replay cutoff, so climatology history is a labelled retrospective benchmark input, not strict point-in-time evidence.

sources.run: IFS run initialised 00:00 UTC on D-1 (the day before each target WIB day), hourly precipitation summed over the target WIB day.
sources.note: Run initialisation time precedes cutoff; exact publication time is not recorded per-run by Open-Meteo. Open-Meteo documents global-model latency of typically 4-6 hours, so a 00:00 UTC run is expected available ~04:00-06:00 UTC, before the 16:55 UTC cutoff. This availability is an INFERENCE, not strict proof; the meteo input is therefore labelled a retrospective/inference benchmark input, never the target day's realized precipitation.
